{{Quote|Though it is assumed that MI-726 has developed deep, troubling glitches due to infrequent memory wipes, sentient accomplices are not being ruled out.|Part of a bounty posting on MI-726|<ref name="BTDF" />}}
'''MI-726''' was an [[MI-series security droid]] belonging to a [[Unidentified Sienar Fleet Systems board member|board member]] of the [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Fleet Systems]] company. During an [[Attack on a Sienar Fleet Systems board member's home|attack]] on the board member's house, the [[Security droid/Legends|security droid]] went rogue and vanished, eventually resurfacing to begin attacking [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] targets. The [[Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations/Legends|Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations]] then posted a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] of 100,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] on the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] for anyone who could destroy the criminal automaton.

==Biography==
{{Quote|During this episode, MI-726 went rogue, abandoned its charge, and disappeared.|MI-726's bounty posting describes its disappearance|<ref name="BTDF" />}}
[[File:Sienar.svg|thumb|right|200px|MI-726 guard a board member of Sienar Fleet Systems.]]
MI-726 was an [[MI-series security droid]]<ref name="BTDF" /> produced by [[Holowan Mechanicals/Legends|Holowan Mechanicals]]<ref name="EV" /> who was assigned to guard the home of a [[Unidentified Sienar Fleet Systems board member|board member]] of the [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Fleet Systems]] [[Starship/Legends|starship]] production company during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. While MI-726 was guarding its owner's home, a group of rebel [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorsits]] [[Attack on a Sienar Fleet Systems board member's home|raided]] the building, hoping to gain access to the schematics of [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]] prototype [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] produced for the Empire. As the house came under attack, MI-726 abandoned the board member and his property, going rogue and fleeing the scene. The [[Security droid/Legends|security droid]] was not seen again for several [[Standard year/Legends|years]], after which it resurfaced and began attacking Imperial warehouses and factories as well as Imperial citizens. During one such [[Attack on an Imperial factory|attack]], a [[Unidentified security guard|security guard]] working at an [[Unidentified Imperial factory (MI-726)|Imperial factory]] encountered MI-726, who insulted the man's heritage and legitimacy before setting off an explosion that destroyed the facility but left the guard alive.<ref name="BTDF" />

The guard reported his encounter with the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] and claimed it was not working alone, a statement that the [[Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations/Legends|Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations]] used in a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] posting for the droid on the [[Imperial Enforcement DataCore/Legends|Imperial Enforcement DataCore]]. The bounty posting offered a 100,000-[[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credit]] reward for any [[Bounty hunter/Legends|individual]] holding an [[Imperial Peace-Keeping Certificate/Legends|Imperial Peace-Keeping Certificate]] who could destroy the droid. The posting described MI-726 as dangerous and speculated the droid was suffering from "deeply troubling" glitches due to a lack of [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipes]], but it did not rule out the possibility of non-droid accomplices.<ref name="BTDF" />

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|The witness claims that the droid insulted his heritage and legitimacy before setting off an explosion that destroyed the entire factory.|A bounty posting on MI-726 gives an eyewitness's account of the droid|<ref name="BTDF" />}}
MI-726 went rogue during an attack on its owner and then turned on those whom it had once served. The droid verbally berated at least one victim during its attacks on Imperials but did not kill the man he insulted. As well as knowledge of the Empire, the droid also had a reasonable knowledge of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. MI-726 was bipedal in stature, [[Color/Legends|silver]] in color, and possessed a pair of large lower [[Limb/Legends|arms]] ending in three&ndash;fingered fists and a pair of smaller upper arms that ended in [[Repeating blaster/Legends|repeating blasters]], which it used in combat, although it could also use demolitions.<ref name="BTDF" />

The droid also possessed red [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]], which it could use with a degree of skill to search rooms and spot particular objects, as well as equipment that allowed it to listen. MI-726 was also equipped with silver [[Armor/Legends|armor]], which at one stage began to rust&ndash;although this did not stop the droid from being able to move silently&ndash;and a [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulator]], with which it was capable of speaking [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]]. The droid could also read and write that [[Language/Legends|language]].<ref name="BTDF" />

==Behind the scenes==
MI-726 was created as part of the ''[[Bounties to Die For]]'' article in the [[Star Wars Gamer 6|sixth issue]] of [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine series, which were supplements for the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="BTDF" /> The issue was released on [[September 4]], [[2001]].<ref name="SW.com">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20010815.html|text=Hunting Down ''Gamer'' #6}}</ref> The article was written by [[S. Mitch Ritchie]] and illustrated by [[Ramón Pérez]], and it provided [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] attributes for MI-726 to allow for its use as an enemy or ally in the game. The article did not specify the era of play in which MI-726 was active to allow for the droid's use in multiple eras, although the Galactic Empire issued MI-726's bounty posting, so the events must take place during the Empire's existence.<ref name="BTDF" />
